findings.title: Server-confirmed message is indistinguishable from the optimistic one
findings.failure_scenario: InMemoryChat.send (Sources/ChatClient/InMemoryChat.swift:65-66) builds the echoed Message from the same id, conversationID and text plus sentAt: now(), and the test passes now: { fixedNow }, which is also the date.now dependency (test line 26). So the server message equals sent("Hello") exactly. If ThreadFeature.swift:121-122 kept the local item's message and emitted it instead of the server message, sendConfirm (and the other send tests) would still pass. The retry brief asked for the server-confirmed message to be asserted after the response.
findings.evidence: ThreadFeatureTests.swift:99 `InMemoryChat(conversations: [Self.ada], now: { fixedNow })`; :105 and :109 both `store.receive(.delegate(.lastMessageChanged(sent("Hello"))))`; :107 only mutates delivery. ThreadFeature.swift:121 `state.items[id: id] = Item(message: message, delivery: .sent)`, :122 `.send(.delegate(.lastMessageChanged(message)))`. InMemoryChat.swift:66 `sentAt: now()`.
findings.fix: Make the backend's now differ from the dependency date (for example fixedNow + 5) and expect that server message in the second delegate and in the item state.
findings.verification_note: I read ThreadFeature.swift, the tests, and InMemoryChat.send. The echoed message differs from the optimistic one only in sentAt, and the backend's now and the dependency date are both fixedNow, so the two messages are equal. Swapping in the local message at lines 121-122 would leave every assertion unchanged, so this test cannot catch that mutation. It is a test gap, not a user-facing defect, so minor (no-harm-yet) stays. I cited lines 105-109, which hold both delegate assertions.

findings.title: Retry guard only tested against .sent, not .sending
findings.failure_scenario: If the guard at ThreadFeature.swift:115 were loosened from `case .failed = item.delivery` to `item.delivery != .sent` (this compiles, because Delivery is Equatable), a Retry on a .sending item would start a second deliver effect. retryIgnoredUnlessFailed only retries a .sent item (line 165) and a .failed one (line 166). No other test sends retryButtonTapped for a .sending item: reloadKeepsPending has one but never retries it. So the mutation survives. No test covers a retry that fails again either: retryWithoutDuplicate and retryIgnoredUnlessFailed both succeed on the retry.
findings.evidence: ThreadFeatureTests.swift:159-162 items are `.sent` and `.failed(.server)` only; :165 `retryButtonTapped(other)` targets the .sent item. ThreadFeature.swift:115 `guard let item = state.items[id: id], case .failed = item.delivery else { return .none }`.
findings.fix: Add a .sending item and send .retryButtonTapped for it with no state change expected. Add a retry that fails again and stays .failed.
findings.verification_note: I traced every retryButtonTapped in the test file (lines 141, 165, 166). None targets a .sending item, and every retry succeeds. The loosened guard would let a .sending item through and every existing test would still pass. It is a test gap with no current user-facing failure, because the shipped guard is correct, so minor (no-harm-yet) stays. I cited the whole test, lines 153-171.

notes:
Retry fix only. Every delegate receive in ThreadFeatureTests now asserts the full .delegate(.lastMessageChanged(message)) payload. I added a trimsText test that sends draft "  Hi \n" and expects the text "Hi". The slice gate is GREEN, and prove reports 8 of 8 changed tests failing with the source reverted.
